posts.title: Why Timber Frame Construction Lasts Generations
posts.excerpt: Discover the ancient art of mortise and tenon joinery and why it creates structures that stand the test of time.
posts.author: Woodly Team
posts.content:
When you invest in a Woodly Co. light post, you're not just buying outdoor lighting — you're investing in a piece of craftsmanship that will outlast most modern construction.

## The Secret: Mortise and Tenon Joinery

For thousands of years, master craftsmen have used mortise and tenon joints to create structures that last centuries. This technique involves cutting a projection (tenon) on one piece of wood to fit precisely into a hole (mortise) in another piece.

Unlike nails or screws that can loosen over time, mortise and tenon joints actually get stronger as the wood seasons and tightens around the joint.

## Why It Matters for Your Light Post

Our 11×11 inch timber posts are built using these same traditional methods. Here's why that matters:

- **No metal fasteners to rust** — The joint itself holds everything together
- **Natural flexibility** — Wood expands and contracts with seasons; the joint moves with it
- **Repairable** — If damage ever occurs, traditional joinery can be restored

## Built for Alabama Weather

From summer heat to winter storms, our posts are finished with UV-resistant protective coatings that work with the natural durability of the timber frame construction.

Interested in seeing our joinery up close? [Visit our workshop](/contact) or [browse our gallery](/gallery) to see completed installations.

posts.title: Solar or Electric: Choosing the Right Power for Your Light Post
posts.excerpt: We offer two power options for our handcrafted light posts. Here's how to decide which is right for your property — including what to expect across the seasons.
posts.author: Woodly Team
posts.content:
One of the most common questions we hear from customers is: *"Which power option should I choose?"* At Woodly, we offer two options — **solar with battery** and **hardwired electric**. The right choice depends on your property, placement, and how you want your light to perform year-round.

## Solar-Powered Light Posts (with Battery)

**Best for:** Driveways, garden paths, and anywhere electrical access is limited.

Our solar posts use a panel to charge an integrated battery during the day. At dusk, the light automatically turns on and runs off stored battery power through the night.

**Pros:**
- Zero operating cost after installation
- No wiring required — install anywhere with sun exposure
- Environmentally friendly
- Automatic dusk-to-dawn operation

**Considerations:**
- Requires good sun exposure for optimal charging
- Battery replacement every 3-5 years depending on use

## How Seasons Affect Solar Charging

Alabama gets plenty of sunshine, but daylight hours change significantly across the year — and that affects how your solar post performs.

**Summer (June):**
- ~14 hours of daylight
- Long charging window, shorter nights
- Battery easily stays topped off
- Peak performance season

**Winter (December):**
- ~10 hours of daylight
- Shorter charging window, longer nights
- Battery works harder to last until dawn
- Positioning matters more — avoid shaded spots

**The good news:** Our solar systems are sized to handle Alabama winters. As long as your post gets 4-6 hours of direct sunlight, it will perform reliably year-round. In deep winter, you might notice slightly dimmer output toward dawn — but for most installations, it's barely noticeable.

**Tip:** If your driveway entrance is heavily shaded by trees (especially evergreens), hardwired electric may be the better choice.

## Hardwired Electric Light Posts

**Best for:** Heavily shaded locations, security lighting, or when you want maximum brightness and reliability regardless of weather or season.

Hardwired posts connect directly to your home's electrical system. They deliver consistent, bright illumination every night — no charging required.

**Pros:**
- Brightest, most consistent light output
- Works in any location, even full shade
- No batteries to replace
- Can integrate with smart home systems, timers, or motion sensors
- Ideal for security lighting

**Considerations:**
- Requires professional electrical installation
- Ongoing energy costs (though LED fixtures keep this minimal)
- Less flexibility if you want to relocate the post later

## Our Recommendation

For most Alabama homeowners with a sunny driveway entrance, **solar with battery** is the way to go. The installation savings are significant, and our sunshine is reliable enough to keep your post glowing year-round.

If your property is heavily wooded, your entrance faces north, or you need rock-solid security lighting, **hardwired electric** is worth the extra installation cost.

Not sure which is right for your property? [Contact us for a free consultation](/contact) — we're happy to visit your site and make a recommendation based on your specific situation.

---

*Every Woodly light post is handcrafted using traditional timber frame joinery, regardless of which power option you choose. The craftsmanship stays the same — only the technology inside changes.*

posts.title: 5 Ways a Wooden Light Post Transforms Your Curb Appeal
posts.excerpt: First impressions matter. Here's how a handcrafted wooden light post can elevate your home's entrance and set your property apart.
posts.author: Woodly Team
posts.content:
They say you never get a second chance at a first impression. When visitors, neighbors, or potential buyers pull up to your home, what do they see? A handcrafted wooden light post at the end of your driveway makes a statement before anyone reaches your front door.

## 1. It Creates a Sense of Arrival

There's something special about turning onto a driveway marked by a beautiful timber post. It signals that you've arrived somewhere intentional — a home where details matter.

Unlike generic metal lamp posts or plastic solar stakes, a wooden light post says *"Welcome. This place is cared for."*

## 2. It Adds Warmth to Your Landscape

Metal and plastic feel industrial. Wood feels like home.

The natural grain, the warm tones, the way it weathers gracefully over time — a wooden post complements gardens, stone pathways, and natural landscaping in a way synthetic materials simply can't.

## 3. It Stands Out (In the Best Way)

Drive through any neighborhood and you'll see the same mass-produced fixtures repeated house after house. A handcrafted timber post is different. It's a conversation starter, a piece of craftsmanship that neighbors notice and remember.

*"Where did you get that light post?"* — You'll hear it more than you expect.

## 4. It Increases Property Value

Real estate professionals consistently list outdoor lighting and landscaping among the top curb appeal investments. A quality wooden light post checks both boxes:

- **Functional lighting** — Safety and visibility at night
- **Architectural detail** — Visual interest that photographs well
- **Quality craftsmanship** — Signals a well-maintained property

Whether you're planning to sell or simply want to enjoy your investment, curb appeal pays dividends.

## 5. It Reflects Your Personal Style

Every Woodly post is built to order. Want a rustic, weathered look? We can do that. Prefer clean lines and a contemporary finish? We've got you covered. The wood species, stain, and fixture style all come together to match *your* vision.

Your home is unique. Your light post should be too.

---

Our timber light posts are handcrafted in Pell City, Alabama using traditional mortise and tenon joinery. Each one is built to last generations.

posts.title: Where to Place Your Driveway Light Post: A Practical Guide
posts.excerpt: Placement matters more than you think. Here's how to choose the perfect spot for your light post based on your driveway, landscaping, and power source.
posts.author: Woodly Team
posts.content:
You've decided on a handcrafted wooden light post — great choice. Now comes the question we hear almost as often as *"solar or electric?"*: **Where exactly should it go?**

Placement affects everything — how your post looks during the day, how well it lights your driveway at night, and even how your power source performs. Here's what we've learned from hundreds of installations across Alabama.

## Start at the Street

The most popular placement is at the entrance to your driveway where it meets the road. There's a reason for that:

- **Visibility** — Guests and delivery drivers can find your home easily after dark
- **Curb appeal** — It's the first thing people see when approaching your property
- **Safety** — Illuminating the transition from road to driveway helps prevent accidents

For most homes, placing the post 2-3 feet back from the road edge and 1-2 feet off the driveway is the sweet spot. Close enough to light the entrance, far enough to stay clear of traffic and mowing equipment.

## One Post or Two?

A single post on one side of the driveway works beautifully for most homes. But if you have a wide entrance — say, 20 feet or more — a matched pair creates a striking gateway effect.

**Single post works best when:**
- Your driveway is standard width (10-16 feet)
- You want a clean, understated look
- Budget is a consideration

**A pair works best when:**
- You have a wide or circular driveway
- Your property has a more formal aesthetic
- You want maximum light coverage at the entrance

## Think About Sun Exposure (Solar Owners)

If you're going with our solar-powered option, placement and sunlight go hand in hand. Your post needs 4-6 hours of direct sunlight daily to keep the battery charged through the night.

Before you commit to a spot, spend a day watching how sunlight moves across your driveway entrance. Pay attention to:

- **Trees** — Even deciduous trees that are bare in winter can block significant light in summer when fully leafed out
- **Buildings** — Your house, garage, or a neighbor's structure might cast afternoon shadows
- **Direction** — South-facing placements get the most consistent sun year-round in Alabama

*If your ideal spot is shaded most of the day, that doesn't mean you're out of luck — it just means [hardwired electric](/blog/solar-or-electric-choosing-the-right-power) is likely the better power choice.*

## Watch Out for Underground Utilities

This one's important. Before you dig, **always call 811** (Alabama's free utility locating service). They'll come mark any buried gas, electric, water, or cable lines on your property — usually within a few business days.

Our posts need a foundation hole roughly 24 inches deep. Hitting a utility line isn't just dangerous; it's an expensive mistake that's completely avoidable with a quick phone call.

## Consider the View from Inside

Here's something most people don't think about until after installation: what does your light post look like from your favorite window?

Walk through your home and look out toward the driveway. The front porch, the kitchen window, the living room — wherever you spend time. A well-placed post adds a warm glow to your evening view. A poorly placed one might be hidden behind a bush or blocked by your car.

## Give It Room to Breathe

Your light post is a piece of craftsmanship. It deserves to be seen. Keep these spacing guidelines in mind:

- **From shrubs and plantings** — At least 3 feet of clearance so foliage doesn't crowd the post as plants grow
- **From the mailbox** — Stagger them rather than clustering. Side by side looks cluttered; 6-8 feet apart looks intentional
- **From fences or walls** — A post gains presence when it stands on its own rather than pressed against a structure

## The Soil Matters Too

Alabama soil varies a lot — from red clay in the Piedmont to sandy loam in the southern counties. The type of soil at your driveway entrance affects how the post is anchored.

- **Clay soil** — Holds well but drains slowly. We may recommend a gravel base in the foundation hole
- **Sandy soil** — Drains well but can shift. A deeper foundation or concrete footing may be needed
- **Rocky ground** — Common around Pell City and the Appalachian foothills. Not a problem, but good to know upfront so we bring the right tools

When you [request a quote](/get-a-quote), let us know about your soil conditions. It helps us plan the right installation approach for your property.

## Our Placement Process

Still not sure where your post should go? That's what our consultation is for. Here's how it works:

1. **Tell us about your property** — Photos, measurements, or just a description
2. **We'll suggest placement options** — Based on your driveway layout, sun exposure, and power preference
3. **You choose** — We'll help you weigh the trade-offs, but it's your property and your vision

We've placed posts at the end of gravel driveways, along winding paved entrances, beside garden pathways, and even flanking barn doors. Every property is different, and that's what makes this work interesting.

---

Ready to figure out the perfect spot? [Get a free quote](/get-a-quote) and we'll help you plan the placement — or [browse our gallery](/gallery) to see how other homeowners have positioned their Woodly posts.
